title: Direct summands of perfect complexes over a ring are perfect
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $K,L$ be objects of the derived category $D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. If $K\oplus L$ is perfect [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], then both $K$ and $L$ are perfect.

proof.text: Put $S=K\oplus L$. By [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], choose a bounded complex $P^\bullet$ of finitely generated projective $A$-modules with $Q(P)\cong S$. Choose integers $a\leq b$ such that $P^i=0$ outside $[a,b]$, enlarging the bounds if necessary. Apply [lem-pc-finite-projective-complex-free-model] to $P$ with upper bound $b$. It gives a bounded-above finite-free complex $F$ and a quasi-isomorphism $F\to P$. Composing its derived isomorphism with $Q(P)\cong S$ shows that $S$ is pseudo-coherent, exactly as defined by [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex].

source.place: Tag 066S, lemma-summands-perfect, using Tag 0658 (lemma-perfect) and Tag 064U (lemma-pseudo-coherent), implication (3) to (1)

proof.text: Choose complex representatives $K_0,L_0$ of $K,L$. Their termwise direct sum represents $S$. The last clause of [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-summand] applies: since $K_0\oplus L_0$ is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded-above finite-free complex, so are $K_0$ and $L_0$. Thus both $K$ and $L$ are pseudo-coherent in the sense of [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex].

Every term $P^i$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat]. The complex $P$ is bounded above, so [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] makes it K-flat. This applies over the given arbitrary commutative ring $A$; neither Noetherianity nor flatness of a test module is required.

For any $A$-module $M$ placed in degree zero, specialize [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] to the identity ring map $A\to A$ and $N=M[0]$. Its K-flat computation clause applied to $P$ identifies $S\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M$ with $Q(P\otimes_A M)$. The latter complex has term $P^i\otimes_A M$ in degree $i$, hence is zero in every degree outside $[a,b]$. Its cohomology there is zero. The same interval works for every $M$, so $S$ has finite Tor dimension with amplitude $[a,b]$.

source.place: Tag 0658 (lemma-perfect), forward implication, and Tag 06Y6 (lemma-derived-base-change), K-flat computation

proof.text: For $T=K$ and then $T=L$, let $i:T\to S$ and $p:S\to T$ be the biproduct inclusion and projection, so $p\circ i=1_T$. For each $M$ and degree $j$, apply the tensor functor of [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] and the cohomology functor of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Functoriality gives $H^j(p\otimes 1)\circ H^j(i\otimes 1)=1_{H^j(T\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M)}$. If $j\notin[a,b]$, these maps factor through $H^j(S\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M)=0$ by Step 4, so the displayed identity is zero. A module whose identity is zero is the zero module. Thus $K$ and $L$ both have Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$. This writes out the summand argument of Tag 066G using the actual inclusion and projection maps.

source.place: Tag 066G (lemma-summands-tor-amplitude), proof by additivity, expanded using retracts

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-finite-tor-perfect] separately to $C=K$ and $C=L$. Step 2 supplies a bounded-above finite-free model, hence in particular a bounded-above finitely generated projective model, and Step 5 supplies the finite Tor interval $[a,b]$. Its conclusion gives a bounded finitely generated projective model for each object. This is perfectness as defined by [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], proving both assertions.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q116-6484b5030 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item in full, the statement of each of the 9 nodes it cites, and the Stacks text of more-algebra.tex at 066S, 0658, 064X, 066G and the tor-amplitude definition. The item statement matches 066S exactly: A is a commutative ring, the objects are in D(A), and perfect means a bounded complex of finitely generated projective modules. The six steps follow the source route of 0658, 064X and 066G. Step 1: the free-model lemma from 064U gives pseudo-coherence. Step 2: the last clause of the ring pseudo-coherence summand lemma (064X). Step 3: projective implies flat (a Mathlib leaf), and a bounded-above flat complex is K-flat (064K). Step 4: the K-flat clause (2) of the derived tensor functor gives one Tor interval [a,b] for every module M. Step 5: the 066G retract argument written out; it is genuinely elementary. Step 6: the ring criterion from 0658, applied to K and to L separately. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses, and there is no cycle. There are no new nodes. The only similar existing nodes (lem-pc-perfect-summand and the thick-closure lemma) are about D(O_X) on a scheme, a different object, so there is no duplicate. I accept the five declared off-unit tool uses; each is a generic algebra lemma that no node of sk-thm-sf-package states. Edge cases checked: A=0, a zero summand, and a projective but non-free summand over a non-Noetherian ring. Two defects in existing nodes need maintenance; neither is in this delivery, so they do not block it. First, lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-finite-tor-perfect links D(R) and 'perfect' to the scheme definitions, although its text and conclusion are explicitly about the ring. Second, lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-summand cites 064T where the tag is 064U. No fixes were written.
